question: Why do children have different nutritional needs compared to adults?

options.A: Children require fewer calories per kilogram of body weight
options.B: Children do not need micronutrients until puberty begins
options.C: Adults have higher metabolic demands than growing children
options.D: Children are actively building new tissue and growing rapidly

explanation: Spot on! Growing kids need extra fuel and building blocks because their bones, muscles, and organs are developing fast. You've got this! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T006#GNS227_U2_T006_h1)

question: Why is tracking a child's growth over several visits better than just taking one weight measurement?

options.A: Children never change their weight during growth spurts
options.B: Growth charts are completely inaccurate for children under five years old
options.C: A steady pattern shows normal development better than one isolated number
options.D: A single measurement only shows fluid balance, not true growth

explanation: Great thinking! Checking growth over time gives you the real trend rather than stressing over a single random number. Nursing is all about the big picture! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T006#GNS227_U2_T006_h1)

question: What is the main job of dietary fats in infants and toddlers?

options.A: Acting as the main fuel source for red blood cells
options.C: Supporting central nervous system development and brain growth
options.D: Supplying all the necessary vitamin C for the immune system

explanation: Exactly! Little ones need healthy fats because their growing brains and nerves depend heavily on them for proper development. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T006#GNS227_U2_T006_h2)

question: A mother asks why her toddler needs a mix of both animal and plant proteins. What's the best way to answer?

options.A: Mixing them ensures the child gets all the essential building blocks for growth
options.B: Animal proteins contain no essential amino acids on their own
options.C: Plant proteins are toxic to the kidneys of young children
options.D: Only animal proteins can provide energy for daily physical activities

explanation: Spot on. Combining different protein sources helps make sure the child gets every essential amino acid their growing body needs! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T006#GNS227_U2_T006_h2)

question: Which mineral shortage causes anemia and makes it hard for children to focus and learn?
explanation: You got it! Iron helps make hemoglobin to carry oxygen around the body. Without enough of it, kids feel tired and find it tough to concentrate. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T006#GNS227_U2_T006_h3)

question: When planning a community program to prevent rickets in toddlers, which two nutrients should you focus on?
explanation: Brilliant! Calcium and Vitamin D are best friends when it comes to building strong, hard bones and preventing rickets. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T006#GNS227_U2_T006_h3)

question: Why do babies and young children dehydrate so quickly when they have an illness like diarrhea?

options.A: Their bodies contain a higher proportion of water and faster metabolism
options.B: Their kidneys concentrate urine much better than adult kidneys do
options.C: They drink significantly more water than adults relative to body size
options.D: Their skin is too thick to absorb sweat and moisture from the air

explanation: Exactly right! Because little ones have more body water and a faster turnover rate, losing fluids affects them much faster than it would an adult. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T006#GNS227_U2_T006_h4)

question: Which of these is an early physical sign that an infant is becoming dehydrated?
explanation: Spot on! When fluid levels drop, those soft spots on top of an infant's head (fontanelles) dip inward. Excellent clinical observation! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T006#GNS227_U2_T006_h4)

question: What is the primary dietary cause of kwashiorkor in children?

options.A: Severe deficiency of protein despite eating enough carbohydrates
options.B: An excess of iron leading to metabolic blockage
options.C: Severe lack of overall calories and total food intake
options.D: Complete lack of dietary fat and essential oils in the diet

explanation: You nailed it! Kwashiorkor happens when a child gets enough starchy food to fill their tummy, but lacks protein, leading to that characteristic swelling. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T006#GNS227_U2_T006_h5)

question: How can you easily tell the difference between a child with marasmus and one with kwashiorkor?

options.A: Marasmus causes high fever and rashes, while kwashiorkor causes breathing failure
options.B: Children with kwashiorkor have no body fat loss at all compared to normal children
options.C: Kwashiorkor only affects teenagers, while marasmus only affects newborn infants
options.D: Marasmus children have severe muscle wasting and look very thin, while kwashiorkor children show pitting edema and swelling

explanation: Great job! Marasmus is like severe starvation with extreme thinness, while kwashiorkor features notable swelling (edema) from lack of protein. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T006#GNS227_U2_T006_h5)

question: What does a low Height-for-Age measurement tell you about a child?

options.A: Temporary weight gain from eating too much sugar
options.C: Chronic malnutrition or stunting over a long period
options.D: Immediate lack of protein causing fluid swelling

explanation: Spot on! Height-for-age is our long-term scorecard. A low score tells us the child has been dealing with poor nutrition over a good while (stunting). [learn more](GNS227_U2_T006#GNS227_U2_T006_h6)

question: Why do community health nurses love using the Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) tape in the field?

options.A: It is quick, easy to use, and does not require complex scales
options.B: It is the only tool that can accurately measure linear height in toddlers
options.C: It gives an exact measurement of the child's total body fat percentage
options.D: It replaces the need to check for clinical signs of vitamin deficiency

explanation: Exactly! MUAC is portable, fast, and practical when you are out in community outreaches screening lots of children quickly. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T006#GNS227_U2_T006_h6)

question: What is the golden rule for feeding an infant during their first six months of life?

options.A: Exclusive breastfeeding with no other foods or liquids
options.B: Cow milk combined with fresh fruit juices
options.C: Formula milk mixed with clean local spring water
options.D: Breastmilk supplemented with thin cereal porridges

explanation: You got it! Breastmilk alone for the first six months provides all the nutrients and infection-fighting protection a baby needs. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T006#GNS227_U2_T006_h7)

question: A community nurse is advising Nigerian mothers on affordable toddler meals. Which approach works best?

options.A: Tell mothers to avoid local vegetables because they lack minerals
options.B: Encourage combining local staples like beans and grains to make balanced meals
options.C: Insist that only imported tinned foods provide enough vitamins for growth
options.D: Advise mothers to feed the child only once a day with a large heavy meal

explanation: Brilliant! Using affordable local foods like beans and maize is sustainable, cost-effective, and keeps our little ones well-nourished. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T006#GNS227_U2_T006_h7)
